summary_text:
Carolina just straight-up dominated Seattle from the opening puck drop at the barn, rolling to a 5-1 win and honestly it wasn't even that close. The shot totals tell the whole story: 32 shots on goal for the Canes versus just 12 for the Kraken. That's not a hockey game, that's a shooting gallery.

First period set the tone. Jackson Blake lit the lamp at 11:12 on the power play, with Sebastian Aho and Nikolaj Ehlers setting the table. Then Mark Jankowski buried one at 17:30 off feeds from Jesperi Kotkaniemi and Sean Walker. CAR put up 8 shots to Seattle's 3 and headed to the room up 2-0. The Canes were cycling and controlling play like it was a practice drill.

Second period got a little loose but Carolina still owned it. Andrei Svechnikov sniped twice — both on the power play, both assisted by Shayne Gostisbehere, with Ehlers adding another apple on the first one. Seattle got one back at 6:06 when Matty Beniers beat Pyotr Kochetkov, with Jordan Eberle and Bobby McMann picking up assists. That was the only real blemish. CAR answered right back and took a 4-1 lead into the third, outshooting Seattle 13-4 in the frame.

Third period was cruise control. Jankowski potted his second of the night at 11:06, Taylor Hall and Seth Jarvis with the helpers. Kochetkov wasn't tested much — 12 shots against all night — but he made the saves when called upon.

Special teams were the difference. CAR went 3-for-5 on the power play and killed off both Seattle chances. That's a recipe for a blowout every time.

This win is part of a serious heater. Carolina has now won four of five, including two straight against Seattle and a 9-2 demolition of Chicago earlier in the week. The only loss was that 4-1 dud against Nashville. When the power play hums like this and the shot volume is that lopsided, the Canes are a problem for anybody.
card_text: CAR 5-1 over Seattle, and the Canes' power play was straight-up filthy — three goals on the man advantage. Svechnikov sniped a pair, Jankowski lit the lamp twice, and Ehlers set the table all night. That's four straight wins and a 5-1 shellacking at home.
